roads.name: Stratford High Street
roads.alignmentEvidence: T13 retrace (October 2026): centreline re-read on the OS London five-foot (1:1056) 1893-96 mosaic, NLS layer os-london-five-foot-1893, zoom 18 (about 0.37 m per pixel) as the midpoint between the two inner rails of the double horse-tram track drawn in the carriageway (four parallel rail lines, track centres about 2.70 m apart). The rail centres were detected automatically in cross-profiles every 1 m and checked by eye at every bridge; a robust spline was fitted through them, with a separate fit either side of the sheet join east of St Michael's Bridge, and the route keeps a vertex wherever the spline departs from the chord by more than 0.10 m. Where lettering or the railway viaduct hides the rails (about 790-850 m and 1080-1120 m along the route) the spline bridges gaps of up to 30 m on straight carriageway. Measured: route within 0.02 m median, 1.85 m maximum of the detected rail centre at the 106 ten-metre stations where the rails are legible. Estimated: the 12 m carriageway width (the drawn kerb lines are not continuous enough to measure; the frontage-to-frontage space is 15-18 m including footways), paving and levels. Scene origin 538900,183209.

bridgeSpans.alignmentEvidence: T13 retrace (October 2026): span laid on the retraced High Street centreline, on a straight piece of the route so the deck axis is the road axis. OS reading: bank lines read by eye at both parapets on 6-9x crops: the west bank crosses the centreline at 97.7 m along the route (34 deg from square to the road) and the east bank at 122.5 m (10 deg); the channel axis is 22 deg from square, so the road crosses the River Lea obliquely, as drawn, and the bridge carries it straight across. The span runs from 91.2 m to 123.4 m along the route so the 14.2 m deck (carriageway plus 1.1 m footways) covers the model water and its 0.6 m clearance across the full width; at the centreline the span ends lie -6.5 m and +0.9 m from the bank lines; the excess is the 0.6 m water clearance plus the skew of the banks across the deck width (the model water outline also starts 2.3 m west of the read west bank). Previous span (priorPoints) was 39.2 m long, 2.6 deg off the retraced road axis, its ends -2.1 m and -0.5 m to the side of the retraced centreline. Estimated: arch form, deck height and the abutment faces, which docs/infrastructure.js draws square to the road.

roads.name: Marshgate Lane
roads.alignmentEvidence: T18 retrace (October 2026) on the OS London five-foot plan revised 1893-96 (NLS tiles reference/nls-tiles/os-london-five-foot-1893, read with scripts/factory_map_sources.py mosaic() in straightened strips and cross-profiles along the prior centreline). Mapped: the printed carriageway edges, which are the dotted kerb lines where the plan draws them and otherwise the printed building or wall face that bounds the carriageway (the east face of the lane from the High Street to the bridge, and the west face of St Thomas Mills at the north end); the centreline is their midpoint at 53 stations every 2 m. Fit: median 0.067 m, largest 0.281 m from those midpoints (prior trace: median 3.75 m, largest 6.6 m; it ran up to 1.5 m inside the printed P.H. at the High Street corner and along the house fronts west of the lane further north). The High Street end now meets the High Street centreline. Estimated: the 7 m modelled width (the printed carriageway is 3.4-6.5 m between kerbs), and the line across the High Street corner, where no kerb is printed. The lane now ends in the forecourt in front of St Thomas Mills (printed spot height 16.5): the prior trace ran on for 39 m through the printed house row west of the lane to the mill; the printed passage beside the mill is only about 4.4 m between building faces, and a 7 m carriageway with footways there would stand in the modelled mill (site257-mill, whose footprint lies about 1.5 m west of the printed mill face), so that passage is not modelled. The provisional connection deck keeps its prior stations along the lane and moves with it. Readings and overlays: T18_REPORT.md.

OS reading: bank lines read by eye at both parapets on 6-9x crops: the west bank crosses the centreline at 97.7 m along the route (34 deg from square to the road) and the east bank at 122.5 m (10 deg); the channel axis is 22 deg from square, so the road crosses the River Lea obliquely, as drawn, and the bridge carries it straight across. The span runs from 91.2 m to 123.4 m along the route so the 14.2 m deck (carriageway plus 1.1 m footways) covers the model water and its 0.6 m clearance across the full width; at the centreline the span ends lie -6.5 m and +0.9 m from the bank lines; the excess is the 0.6 m water clearance plus the skew of the banks across the deck width (the model water outline also starts 2.3 m west of the read west bank). Previous span (priorPoints) was 39.2 m long, 2.6 deg off the retraced road axis, its ends -2.1 m and -0.5 m to the side of the retraced centreline. Estimated: arch form, deck height and the abutment faces, which docs/infrastructure.js draws square to the road.

segments.evidence: Outside the core box: held at the unchanged northern connection formation (5.5 m) to the east depot junction at chainage 70, whose sidings cross the northern connection bank at that level (scripts/east_depot_tracks.py).

Interpreted, not mapped: from the depot junction the line falls about 1:26 to the measured level crossing at Abbey Road. The OS draws no embankment here (fence-line ground 14.4-14.8 ft at chainage 74 and 121) and shows the northern connection at grade under Stratford Bridge, so this ramp is a model joint between the revised branch and the unrevised connection and depot, not history; it stands up to about 2.6 m above the OS ground inside the box (chainage 107-176).

Mapped: no embankment hatching along the branch in the core box; a level crossing at Abbey Road (S.B.); the walled band and the Northern Outfall Sewer aqueduct carried over the line; Manor Road beside it at 5.3-8.4 ft; Lower Abbey Mills Junction with the curve; Manor Road carried over the line on a bridge at about chainage 1262. Formation levels from the OS level register (data/maps/railway-levels.json): bridge -16.8-103.4 m; embankment 103.4-290 m; at-grade 290-700 m; embankment 700-902.8 m; bridge 902.8-944.0 m; embankment 944.0-959.0 m.
railways.routeEvidence: Retraced on the OS five-foot plan (scripts/factory_map_sources.py mosaic): east of Abbey Creek wharf the four drawn rails of the two running lines lie on one straight line (13 cross-sections from chainage 600 to 890, RMS 0.05 m about the line through scene (-2.8, 361.89) bearing (0.9287, -0.3707)). The prior trace ran along the southern slope hatching, 1.1 m south of the rails at chainage 600, 6 m at 700, 11.5 m at 800 and 15.1 m at 890. The route keeps its first four points (Bow Creek to Abbey Creek wharf, within 1.5 m of the drawn rails) and then follows that line across the bridge over the G.E.R. Woolwich branch and Manor Road to 15 m past its east abutment; the OS shows the line continuing east on embankment beyond.

basis: level with the west-end rail reading (approach behind the west abutment)
deck level carried to the east abutment face
level approach east of the bridge to the route end

segments.evidence: Measured: three rail-level readings 25.4-25.6 ft on the Bow Creek bridge and its east abutment (formation 5.05-5.11 m). The model keeps its two crossings here (Bow Creek, chainage 0-36, and the second channel, 68-95) with embankment between; the OS draws one continuous structure from the west bank to the east abutment at about chainage 103.

Mapped: embankment hatching both sides from the bridge to about chainage 290. Measured: bank top 21.9 ft at 176 and 18.9 ft at 253. Interpolated: linear between them (1:120 and 1:85) and on to the first at-grade reading.

Mapped: no embankment hatching past the goods shed, Hempleman's manure works (site 1018), Abbey Creek wharf and Upper Abbey Mills Junction. Measured: ground and yards beside the line 10.7-16.3 ft. Interpreted: formation 0.1 m above the ground readings, linear between them (falling 1:100 to the wharf, then level within 0.1 m). Bench marks on walls beside the line (14.68 ft on the railway boundary, 15.94 ft at the manure works) stand 0.3-1 m above the ground and are checks, not controls.

Mapped: embankment hatching both sides from about chainage 700 to the bridge, with the foot at 7.5-7.9 ft. Measured: bank top 19.9 ft at the bridge (on the bank 25 m north of the line). Interpolated: rising 1:96 from the last at-grade level to the bridge.

Mapped: the line crossing the G.E.R. Woolwich branch (four rails, scene x 247-252) and Manor Road (x 256-270) on a bridge between abutment faces at x 231.9 and 270.2 on the retraced centreline (chainage 902.8-944.0); B.M. 5.46 ft on the pier between the railway and the road (x 257.5, chainage 930.4). Interpreted: the deck level is the bank top at the west abutment, carried level; two spans on one pier; deck and girder form as the model's other plain-railway crossings.
Mapped: embankment hatching continuing east past the route end. Interpreted: level approach 15 m past the east abutment, closed by the main landscape's earth end (the line beyond is not modelled).

under.basis: rail top of the traced Great Eastern Railway, Woolwich branch at its chainage 661.3 (the trace runs about 12 m east of the OS rails here, under the Manor Road span)
highest OS road reading under the span

railways.name: Abbey Mills junction curve
railways.evidence: Route traced from OS; track spacing, sleepers and level are schematic. Formation levels from the OS level register (data/maps/railway-levels.json): low bank 0-408.4 m.
railways.routeEvidence: First point moved 1.8 m onto the retraced LT&SR (the projection of the prior junction point), so the curve leaves the LT&SR on its centreline at Upper Abbey Mills Junction; the rest of the trace is unchanged.

basis: LT&SR formation at Upper Abbey Mills Junction (LT&SR chainage 634.8)
Woolwich branch formation at Lower Abbey Mills Junction (branch chainage 1011.2)

segments.evidence: Mapped: two tracks from Upper to Lower Abbey Mills Junction with a narrow stippled bank on the outside of the curve and marsh 4.5-4.9 ft inside it. No rail level is given. Interpolated: linear between the two junction levels (falling about 1:200), so both junctions meet at one level; the bank height above the marsh falls from about 2 m to nothing.

railways.name: Great Eastern Railway — main line
railways.evidence: Corridor traced from the georeferenced OS map, behind East London Soap Works and City Mills toward Stratford. Four continuous running tracks are an initial representation, not a completed siding/junction diagram. Heights, slopes, bridge architecture and track spacing interpreted; local rise clears the existing model sewer crest.

mainlineExtension.evidence: Bounded continuation along supplied GE mainline beyond the former cropped endpoint. Original route/station prefix and chainages remain exact; append a smooth tangent transition, and restore the OS-confirmed low-level underpass opening without changing the four original track profiles.
mainlineExtension.sourceAlignmentEvidence: Retain the OS-authored GE endpoint and tangent exactly; reconcile its25.885m offset to the generalized GIS within the bounded85m continuation. The new endpoint lies on the supplied GIS centreline.

railways.name: Great Eastern Railway — Woolwich branch northern connection

source.map: Archived NLS OS London five-foot map, 1893 revision / 1894 publication
source.registration: Georeferenced NLS tiles; first point aligned to the outer main-line track pair and last point to the existing branch.

railways.evidence: Mapped Woolwich-branch curve and running-line corridor south past Stratford Market. Two tracks, a smooth grade to the main line, bridge girders and earth slopes are interpreted; this is not a complete Stratford track/signalling plan.
railways.alignmentNote: The old independently registered northern branch endpoint was 28.37 m east of the mapped rail corridor. Shift it west and blend into the next existing station, avoiding the Bridge Road terrace frontage.

eastChannelseaRailAlignment.review: Native OS running-line corridor east of Stratford Market roof79 and shaded station body1539. Re-read seven controls12–18; station controls12–15 follow the running pair between station bodies. Mainline join/curve controls0–11 and branch tail19–20 retained. Gauge, spacing, formation profile and join levels retained. Mapped station bodies bound only interpreted bank toes; unresolved booking-office bridge approach keeps rail support.

stationFormationReview.evidence: Native OS running rails east of the shaded western station body1539 and between the northern waiting-room/platform bodies. Station formation slopes stop at these mapped bodies. No roof height, new retaining wall, platform architecture or complete station track layout is asserted.
stationFormationReview.bookingLimit: Booking-office bodies at the road bridge span the apparent rail approach. Their precise over-track function/height remains unresolved; the interpreted running crest and a0.51m shoulder survive here. Source intersection is not permission to move native rails or remove their support.

railways.name: North London / Victoria Park branch connection
railways.source: Repository Rail_1895.geojson, WGS84 reprojected through BNG; local x=E-538900,z=183209-N

junction.interpretation: Native OS independently reviewed: Victoria Park rails terminate at the west edge of the continuous diagonal GE rails and resume east at Stratford Station Low Level. No diamond/turnout across the main; interpreted underpass retained.

mainlineExtension.evidence: Bounded continuation along supplied GE mainline beyond the former cropped endpoint. Original route/station prefix and chainages remain exact; append a smooth tangent transition, and restore the OS-confirmed low-level underpass opening without changing the four original track profiles.

railways.evidence: GIS ways retain the missing northwestern route and upper Woolwich continuation. Native OS shows Victoria Park Branch, Central/Fork Junction and Stratford Station Low Level. The existing southern connector chord remains a separate route. Exact historical rail levels, turnout arrangement and construction are unresolved.
railways.levelEvidence: Interpreted lower formation3.0m at the OS-confirmed underpass, smoothly joining the existing Woolwich station. Existing GE formation8.5m yields4.39m from lower rail head to upper deck soffit; exact historical elevations remain unmeasured.

sewerHighStreet.levelEvidence: Provisional surface profile only, not sewer invert or hydraulic gradient. OS reads 24.7 ft on High Street near the crossing and BM 22.40 at St Michael; 3.5 m matches their relative difference against the existing 2.8 m bridge datum. Wider ground datum and cover depths not calibrated.

surfacePolicy: Macadam for residential streets; clinker/earth for working lanes and paths; selected cartage/works approaches modelled with granite setts. No wood-block street identified, no modern tarmac, no electrified tram infrastructure. Assignments do not establish council adoption status.

districtNotes: High Street bridge names follow the 19th-century transposition: Pegshole over Three Mills Back River; St Thomas over western Waterworks arm; St Michael over eastern arm.
Bow Bridge: one granite-faced span completed 1839. c1900 appearance retained; 1901–06 construction stages unresolved.
User-supplied 1851 guide illustration and Mackenzie painting show the earlier multi-arch bridge, retained as historical comparison only.
St Thomas brick arch count is not established by the written source; one opening is a modelling estimate.
Surface materials, widths and heights are estimates. No 1933 Groves Bridge or modern flyover.

Three provisional lane connections cover small discrepancies between road tracing and independently registered GIS banks at Marshgate Lane, Cook’s Road and the Three Mills yard. Their deck/culvert structure is unresolved, unlike the five documented High Street bridges.
housingNotes: Street-facing envelopes and junction breaks audited together. Rear plots are not treated as lanes. Widths and facades remain approximate; see housing-road-traces.json for corrections and omissions.
